Keep selection lines visible in the pull request log

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Python and JavaScript app configures `uv run pytest && npm test | tee tests.log` and adopts the doctor’s suggested `fast_test`.
The shell-flow check returns no parts for the entire command. Because a Python manifest exists, `quicktest.py:107-108` then suggests only `forge test --pytest {base}`. On a JavaScript-only change, `pytest_tests` also sees no parts and returns success without running npm (`fasttest.py:699-704, 753-757`). The pull request check uses `fast_test` when set (`review.py:368-372`), so it can pass without running the JavaScript tests.
findings.title: Preserve JavaScript tests in advice for a piped mixed command

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - An app runs separate Playwright projects, such as `playwright test --project=chromium && playwright test --project=firefox`, and adopts the doctor’s suggestion.
The second Playwright step is discarded because its runner kind has already been seen (`quicktest.py:89-90`). Since the pull request check also uses `fast_test` when configured (`review.py:368-372`), Firefox coverage is omitted. The same advice path also appends `--only-changed` to a compound npm script at line 100, where npm forwards it to the last command rather than necessarily to Playwright.
findings.title: Keep distinct Playwright steps in the suggested fast command

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A client has `cd backend && pytest tests` with `forge.toml` at the repository root.
The replacement starts the picker after `cd`, but `pytest_tests` reads `Path("forge.toml")` from its current directory at `fasttest.py:718`. It raises `FileNotFoundError` before selecting or running tests, failing close or the pull request check. New evidence beyond the directory ruling is that the picker still requires the root settings file; the existing scenario in `tests/test_testplace_selection.py:137-174` has this layout.
findings.title: Keep the repository settings available to pytest after cd

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - An Nx test command uses project filters, task arguments, or environment variables.
The rewrite preserves `--projects` even though [Nx documents that filter for run-many, not affected](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-commands), so the original project restriction is lost. It also appends `--base` after an existing `--`, making it a task argument, and shell-quotes values such as `--configuration=$MODE`, preventing expansion. These valid commands can run the wrong projects or fail after conversion.
findings.title: Preserve Nx argument semantics when rewriting run-many

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repository has a compound `test` script and also runs `playwright test` directly, or runs `npm test` after `cd web`.
This check treats any matching word in a command as an invocation of a package script. A compound root `test` script therefore makes a separate `playwright test` run whole. Separately, classification is performed before tracking `cd` and reads only the root package (`fasttest.py:280`, `quicktest.py:25-26, 47-51`). If the root test script uses Vitest and the web script uses Playwright, Forge passes Vitest flags to Playwright and fails the check.
findings.title: Bind npm script detection to the invoked script and directory

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Python app runs `pytest tests/unit && pytest tests/integration`, and the change affects only a unit test.
Each replacement calls the repository-wide picker, which selects the unit test for both steps (`fasttest.py:721, 753-760`). The integration invocation still runs, but all of its files are excluded, so pytest exits with no tests collected and fails the check. With explicit test-file arguments, `narrow_command` can instead remove the second step’s only path and run the selected test again.
findings.title: Select pytest files separately for each pytest step

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Python test command contains a quoted expression such as `pytest -k '(cart or order)'`.
`shlex` removes the quotes, so the argument begins with `(` and this check treats it as shell control flow. `close_tests` consequently runs the whole command instead of the related pytest selection, and a surrounding chain loses its per-step selections too.
findings.title: Keep quoted pytest expressions out of shell-flow detection

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A Python app configures `ruff check src && mypy src && pytest` and changes one file under `src`.
Only a literal `.` is removed before the changed filenames are appended. Both checkers still receive `src` and therefore check the whole directory; the printed selection misleadingly names only the changed file. The new test covers only commands whose original path is `.`.
findings.title: Not done: A Python app without Nx runs only its related pytest tests and checks the changed files.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A fresh CI checkout runs `npm ci && ./node_modules/.bin/nx run-many -t test`.
The target-discovery subprocess runs while Forge is constructing the chain, before `npm ci` installs Nx. Discovery fails and the code silently keeps `nx run-many`, so after installation the check runs every project. The generated workflow installs Forge before `forge test --change`, but does not install the app’s Node dependencies first (`prcheck.py:94-110, 249-253`). This misses the owner’s item: “A change to a client app runs lint, typecheck and tests only for the parts it touches, once, in the pull request check, and the log names those parts.”

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A selected test command writes more than 30 lines of output in the pull request check.
These selection lines are printed before the chain runs. `review.test_run` captures the output and returns only its last 30 lines plus skip and gap lines (`review.py:494-498`), so the generated `forge test --change` log loses the selections. A successful run does not print the full-log path either. The quiet recorder fixtures do not expose this loss.
findings.title: Keep selection lines visible in the pull request log
